title: ScRNA-seq unveils the functional characteristics of glioma-associated macrophages and the regulatory effects of chlorogenic acid on the immune microenvironment-a study based on mouse models and clinical practice.
authors: Wang, Jiachen; Li, Shenglan; Chen, Yuxiao; Chen, Jinyi; Wang, Can; Kang, Zhuang; Huang, Mengqian; Cai, Zehao; Fan, Yuxiang; Lan, Yanjie; Yu, Yumeng; Bai, Ruijing; Chen, Feng; Jiang, Jiandong; Li, Wenbin
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过scRNA-seq和分子对接探讨绿原酸对胶质瘤免疫微环境中巨噬细胞的调控，虽含分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作核心，与本课题无关。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Glioma is the most common primary malignant brain tumor. Despite advances in surgical techniques and treatment regimens, the therapeutic effects of glioma remain unsatisfactory. Immunotherapy has brought new hope to glioma patients, but its therapeutic outcomes are limited by the immunosuppressive nature of the tumor microenvironment (TME). This study aimed to reveal the subpopulations and functional characteristics of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and explore the regulatory effects of chlorogenic acid (CHA) on the immune microenvironment, as well as its potential for clinical application. METHODS: In this study, CHA was used in model mice. ScRNA - seq analysis was conducted to elucidate the differentiation trajectories and functional characteristics of bone marrow - derived monomacrophages (BMDMs) and microglia. A PPI and molecular docking model were constructed using the target prediction database. A case of a patient treated with CHA was reviewed. RESULTS: CHA slowed tumor growth in model mice and extended the survival time of mice. It enhanced the antigen - presenting function of macrophages and T - cell immune activation - related gene expression, activated microglia through the JAK - STAT pathway, and improved the antitumor functions. The good affinity of CHA with STAT1 was confirmed. The patient treated with CHA survived for 5 years and 6 months, achieved partial remission (PR) after 9 months of treatment, and remained alive without any new symptoms or toxic side effects. Our study revealed the subtypes and differentiation trajectories of TAMs. CHA significantly improved the immune microenvironment of glioma by modulating the function of BMDMs and microglia. DISCUSSION: This study may provide new insights into targeting the regulation of TME and offer theoretical and practical support for the clinical application of CHA. The results demonstrated the potential of CHA in improving the immune microenvironment and antitumor effects, which could have implications for future glioma treatment strategies.
abstract_zh: 引言：胶质瘤是最常见的原发性恶性脑肿瘤。尽管手术技术和治疗方案不断进步，胶质瘤的治疗效果仍不尽如人意。免疫治疗为胶质瘤患者带来了新的希望，但其治疗效果受到肿瘤微环境（TME）免疫抑制特性的限制。本研究旨在揭示肿瘤相关巨噬细胞（TAMs）的亚群和功能特征，并探讨绿原酸（CHA）对免疫微环境的调控作用及其临床应用潜力。方法：本研究中，CHA被用于模型小鼠。通过单细胞RNA测序（ScRNA-seq）分析，阐明了骨髓来源单核巨噬细胞（BMDMs）和小胶质细胞的分化轨迹及功能特征。利用靶点预测数据库构建了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）和分子对接模型。回顾了一例接受CHA治疗的患者病例。结果：CHA减缓了模型小鼠的肿瘤生长，并延长了小鼠的生存时间。它增强了巨噬细胞的抗原呈递功能和T细胞免疫激活相关基因的表达，通过JAK-STAT通路激活小胶质细胞，并改善了抗肿瘤功能。CHA与STAT1的良好亲和力得到证实。接受CHA治疗的患者存活了5年6个月，治疗9个月后达到部分缓解（PR），且未出现任何新症状或毒副作用，至今仍存活。我们的研究揭示了TAMs的亚型和分化轨迹。CHA通过调节BMDMs和小胶质细胞的功能，显著改善了胶质瘤的免疫微环境。讨论：本研究可能为靶向调控TME提供新见解，并为CHA的临床应用提供理论和实践支持。结果表明CHA在改善免疫微环境和抗肿瘤效应方面具有潜力，这可能对未来胶质瘤治疗策略产生影响。
